83: the aggregate ends with Thasos, 'still a nominally free state in the time of Pliny' (AD 77); Cliopatria's last year is 83. The Pontic Olbia page, tried for a second date, says nothing of Thasos; no page dates the end of Thasos' free status.
AD 83: Domitian's Chatti war.
AD 84: Agricola at Mons Graupius.

Cliopatria's 84 shape, 116,187 km2 in shapes.csv (about 103,700 km2 in the gazetteer's cells), kept for 84–849 as Cliopatria dates it. 'longer than wide, stretching from Sri Ksetra in the south to Halin in the north', with the Mu valley, the Kyaukse plains and the Minbu region; Tang records '18 Pyu states, nine of which were walled cities, covering 298 districts'.
Cliopatria's 84 shape, with Scotland as far as the Moray Firth (Mons Graupius); the ledger (ledger/62) takes Scotland out in 87

changes.event: data/hierarchy.csv: kingdom-of-kucha vassal of xiongnu ends after 84

captions.text: 85: the Dacian kingdom under King Duras raids Moesia.
85: the fighting ends.
87: Decebalus is crowned king.
AD 87: Rome gives up Scotland.
87: the Xianbei kill the Xiongnu chanyu Youliu.
87 CE: the Xianbei kill the chanyu.
around 88: the Chatti overcome the Cherusci.
around 88: the Chatti defeat Chariomerus and the Cherusci fade from the record.
88: the Romans defeat the Dacians near Tapae.
89: Domitian makes peace.
89: after Domitian's peace Decebalus is a client king of Rome.
89: the great campaign against the Northern Xiongnu.
89: Hami retaken.
89: the Han-Xiongnu contest for the Western Regions ends.
June 89: Dou Xian's expedition.
c. 90 CE: Punjab and Sindh pass to the Kushans.
91: the Northern Xiongnu are driven out.
c. 90: the seat moves from Kapisa to Purushapura (Peshawar) and Mathura.
c. 90: Vima Takto carries the Kushans over the rest of the Indo-Parthian land in north-west India.
c. 90: Mathura and Sialkot enter the Kushan shape.
c. 90: the Haryana, upper Punjab and Kashmir cells that no Cliopatria state held join the Kushan shape with the rest of the 'northwest of South Asia'.
91: Ban Chao takes Kucha and the Protector General's seat.
91: the rest of the Tarim Basin, apart from Yanqi, is drawn as Han.
91: the Protector General sits at Qiuci (Kucha).
91: Wusun land shrinks to Issyk-Kul.
91: the fighting for the plateau ends.
91: the Xianbei occupy the Mongolian Plateau.
91: the Xianbei war ends with the Northern chanyu's flight.
91: Han re-establishes Hami and the protectorate.
91: Ban Chao protector-general.
91: the plateau passes to the Xianbei.
February 91: the last Han pursuit.

the 91 shape without Fergana and Kyrgyzstan; the Tarim, Turfan-Hami and Dzungaria cells are client land; holds 91-105; plus Hami (100 km disc); plus the whole Hexi Corridor (the Four Commanderies of Hexi, Han since 121 BCE)
Sakastan (Sistan, the Helmand and western Arachosia), kept by the Indo-Parthians after the Indian lands were lost
1.71 M km2: the Indus plain, the Punjab, Sindh, Gandhara, Taxila, Mathura, Delhi and Kashmir joined in one year, c. 90 (Vima Takto 'expanded the Kushan Empire into the northwest of South Asia').
the Tarim Basin and Turfan-Hami except Yanqi, with the Protector General at Qiuci (Kucha)

the 84 shape (the Liao-Xing'an steppe) plus the Mongolian Plateau ('the Xianbei began occupying the Mongolian Plateau' in 91) without the Southern Xiongnu's Ordos-Hetao land (Cliopatria's Southern Xiongnu 91 shape); Dzungaria and the Ili stay outside, with the Northern Xiongnu remnant

the Xiongnu who 'remained in Dzungaria near Lake Barkol' after February 91: Dzungaria within the drawn shape and the Pulei (Barkol) side of the Hami circle; Yiwu itself, within 100 km of Hami, is Han from 91 and enters only in 119-125 (ledger)
94: Ban Chao defeats Yanqi and the whole basin submits.
94: Fenghou is acclaimed chanyu of the remnant.
the whole Tarim Basin after the defeat of Yanqi in 94: 'more than fifty kingdoms presented hostages'
